title: How to Hit 7,000 to 10,000 Steps a Day With a Desk Job (No Gym)
intro: You can do it without going to the gym, as long as you break your steps into small sessions throughout the day. Start from your current average and add a little at a time, instead of jumping straight to 10,000.

sections.p: Daily movement like walking burns more energy than most people think. About 7,000 steps can burn 250-350 kcal, depending on your body weight and speed. Sitting at work for 8-9 hours plus traffic really makes your steps drop a lot.
Check last week's average steps in your phone app. If your average is 3,000, aim for 4,000-5,000 first. Add 1,000 every week once you're comfortable.

Use the toilet on another floor and take the stairs up one or two floors. Fill a small water bottle so you get up more often. Ask a colleague to walk for 10 minutes after lunch, and take calls while standing or walking.

Walk around your housing area park before logging in to work. Walk around the house during online meetings with the camera off. For shift workers, walking 10-15 minutes before or after your shift already helps.
Park a bit further from the office or supermarket entrance. If you take the LRT or MRT, get off one station early when the area is safe and the weather is okay. Small steps like these add up fast.

action: Check last week's average steps, then set a target to add 1,000 a day.
Do 3 walking sessions of 10 minutes every day: morning, after lunch and evening.
Set an hourly reminder to get up and walk for 2-3 minutes.
Ask your family to walk for 15 minutes after dinner at least 3 times this week.
Start a weekly step challenge with office friends in a WhatsApp group.
myth: Many people believe walking isn't enough and you must run or do HIIT to lose weight. In reality, walking every day together with controlled eating helps a lot, and it's much easier for busy people to keep up.

faq.a: No exercise burns fat from just one area. Walking helps burn energy overall. When your overall body fat goes down, your tummy will also get smaller bit by bit.
Not necessarily. 10,000 is not a compulsory rule. Going from 4,000 to 7,000 is already a big change for someone with a desk job.

faq.q: Do steps inside the house count?
faq.a: They count. Walking while cooking, tidying up or looking after the kids all adds up. What matters is that your overall total goes up.
